segments.title: Opening: names and work songs on the Angola radio station
segments.summary: Arthur Davis is identified and asked what he does while singing; the room is explained as a prison radio station piping music to the dormitories, dated January 12, 1960.

segments.title: Spelling names and Matthew Maxey at Camp A
segments.summary: Names are spelled, one inmate says he is from Evergreen, Alabama, and Matthew Maxey is said to be at Camp A now.

segments.title: James Russell track and Mosley's age and birthdate
segments.summary: A song by James Russell is played with talk of field-work songs, then the second inmate gives his age and birthdate, May 5, 1926.

segments.title: Learning guitar at Angola; music near Tuskegee
segments.summary: Asked about instruments, he says he learned guitar since coming to Angola, and recalls hearing work songs and Tuskegee Institute music in Alabama.

segments.title: Mule songs played back: Johnny Butler and Louisiana
segments.summary: Allen plays record tracks, including Johnny Butler and a mule song, while the inmates identify singers such as Louisiana, Pete and Thomas.

segments.title: Dr. Oster's return visit and spiritual numbers
segments.summary: They discuss when Dr. Oster at LSU might come back, wanting a Sunday visit, and the spiritual numbers they have for him.

segments.title: Humming on a track and Rodney Mays
segments.summary: The inmates hear themselves humming on a playback, mention a radio-station number and say Rodney Mays knows about it.

segments.title: Work songs while working: quartet, cement, and field gangs
segments.summary: One man describes singing in a spiritual quartet, and they explain what work songs accompany: cement, cutting wood, chopping cotton and corn, and singing to ease labor.

segments.title: Playback of songs including John Henry
segments.summary: Song playback with lyrics, including a John Henry song.

segments.title: Remembering a fellow inmate who died in 1959
segments.summary: A speaker remembers a young inmate who helped the prison and died at Camp A on August 11, 1959, before Oster's expected return; he was 35.

segments.title: Hammer ring track and Oster's first recording visit
segments.summary: They play the hammer ring song, whose lead singer is on the record cover, and recall it as the first song sung when the professor first came.

segments.title: How the hammer song was sung while laying steel
segments.summary: Speakers explain the lead and background singing and that axes beating a log supplied the rhythm for laying track.

segments.title: Closing: leaving the record, learning guitar and fingerpicking in the music school
segments.summary: Allen wraps up and leaves the record; Mosley describes learning to read music and guitar in Angola's music school, his picking technique, and waiting for Oster's promised music.
